experiments.title: Titanic Logistic Baseline
experiments.description:
Hypothesis: Titanic survival is largely driven by sex, class, age and family structure; a regularized linear model on well-engineered features (title extracted from Name, family size, alone flag) with median-imputed Age/Fare plus missing indicators would outperform a raw-feature baseline. A later soft-voting ensemble with ExtraTrees was tested and scored the highest.

Data processing:
- Read local train_data/train.csv (712 labeled rows), validation_data/validation.csv (179 feature-only rows), predict_data/test.csv (418 rows). No external data, no gender_submission.csv.
- Note: the fixed 179-row validation set is supplied pre-split (validation.csv); the earlier re-split of the 712-row train set produced 143 rows and failed evaluation. Corrected to train on all 712 rows and predict the supplied 179-row validation.csv by PassengerId.
- Feature engineering (deterministic, fit-safe): FamilySize=SibSp+Parch+1, IsAlone=(FamilySize==1), Title from Name regex ", ([^.]+)." with Mlle/Ms→Miss, Mme→Mrs, rare→"Rare".
- Preprocessing in a ColumnTransformer fit on training rows only: StandardScaler on numeric (Pclass,SibSp,Parch,FamilySize,IsAlone); Age/Fare median imputation with missing indicator then scaling; Sex/Embarked (missing→'M')/Title one-hot with handle_unknown='ignore'.

Best measured model:
- 0.5 * LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, random_state=42) + 0.5 * ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, min_samples_leaf=4, random_state=42, n_jobs=4). Soft-vote of predict_proba, threshold ≥0.5 → 1. Seed 42, CPU.
- This ensemble scored the engine-recorded best validation metric 0.8492, exceeding the single L1-regularized LR (C tuned, 0.8436) and the earlier RF (0.83), LogFare/wt/Deck/AgeBin variants (≤0.8436).

Validation evidence (executed): The evaluator measured the fixed-split accuracy; the best reported is 0.8492 for the LR+ExtraTrees soft-vote. Single-factor results measured along the way: majority floor ~0.615, sex-only ~0.776, baseline LR ~0.816, +Title/FamilySize/IsAlone ~0.8436, RF ~0.832, LogFare ~0.832, class_weight ~0.827.

Changes from parent: started from an LR baseline using raw Pclass/SibSp/Parch/Sex/Embarked with Age/Fare imputation. Added Name-derived Title, FamilySize, IsAlone, standardized numerics, and finally a soft-voting ExtraTrees ensemble.

Artifacts: predictions.csv (418 rows, PassengerId+Survived, test order), work/val_predictions.csv (179 rows aligned to validation.csv), work/model_blend_et.joblib (dict {"lr","et"}), work/metrics.json, work/README.txt. Earlier single-model artifacts retained: work/model_final.joblib.

Load: joblib.load("work/model_blend_et.joblib"); prob = 0.5*lr.predict_proba(X)[:,1] + 0.5*et.predict_proba(X)[:,1]; Survived = (prob>=0.5).astype(int). Apply the same featurize() to raw rows before predict.
experiments.suggestions:
Observed weaknesses (evidence): The validation set is only 179 rows, so single-trial accuracy swings by ~1–2 points are within noise; the 0.8436→0.8492 gain from the ensemble is plausible but small and could partly be noise. RF, LogFare, class_weight, C-tuning, Deck and AgeBin added no gain; LR on the chosen features is a strong, stable baseline.

Lessons (evidence): (1) The validation set is supplied pre-split; do not re-split the 712-row train file (caused the 143-vs-179 failure). (2) Scaling numerics removed lbfgs convergence warnings without changing accuracy. (3) Tree ensembles only helped as a soft complement to LR (LR+ExtraTrees), not standalone (RF/GB regressed).

Prioritized next experiments (hypotheses, not yet run): (1) Re-tune ExtraTrees depth/leaf and the LR/ET blend weight (0.5 fixed here) via internal 5-fold CV on the 712 train rows — test whether the blend weight and leaf size matter beyond noise. (2) Add a small calibrated HistGradientBoosting as a third voter with weight chosen by CV; verify it beats the two-model blend on the fixed 179-row validation. (3) Calibrate probabilities (Platt/isotonic on internal CV) to check if threshold 0.5 remains optimal for accuracy. (4) Confirm run-to-run stability by varying the ET n_jobs/seed-free components; keep seed 42 and report variance across internal CV folds rather than trusting a single fixed-split number.

experiments.title: CV-tuned blend weights & ET leaves
experiments.description:
**Task & metric.** Binary classification of Titanic `Survived` (0/1). Primary metric is accuracy on the fixed 179-row validation holdout; training uses the evaluator-supplied 712 rows of `train_data/train.csv` only, validation/test are transform-only, and predictions must be 0/1 (prob >= 0.5 -> 1).

**Best measured version (canonical incumbent, fixed-validation accuracy 0.8492 — the best score observed across all executed rounds).** A 50/50 soft-vote blend of two CPU models fit on all 712 training rows:
- LogisticRegression (sklearn default C=1.0, max_iter=2000, random_state=42).
- ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, min_samples_leaf=4, criterion='gini', random_state=42, n_jobs=4).
- Blended probability = 0.5*p_LR + 0.5*p_ET; Survived = 1 if prob >= 0.5 else 0.

**Feature processing (shared ColumnTransformer fit on training rows only, embedded in each pipeline):**
- `FamilySize = SibSp + Parch + 1`, `IsAlone = (FamilySize == 1)`.
- `Title` extracted from `Name` via regex `,\s*([^.]+)\.`; Mlle/Ms -> Miss, Mme -> Mrs; titles with training count < 10 mapped to `Rare`.
- `Embarked` missing -> 'M'.
- Numeric `[Pclass, SibSp, Parch, FamilySize, IsAlone]`: median impute + StandardScaler.
- `[Age, Fare]`: median impute with add_indicator + StandardScaler.
- Categorical `[Sex, Embarked, Title]`: constant 'M' impute + OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore').

**Validation evidence (executed, evaluator-scored):**
- Incumbent achieved 0.8492 on the fixed 179-row holdout (best so far; reproduced byte-identically, val md5 `cceba64816`, test md5 `42c718fef6`).
- Seven controlled perturbations were each executed and all failed to beat 0.8492: round-4 CV-tuned blend (w=0.4, ET d=6/leaf=3) = 0.8436; interaction features (Sex_Pclass, FamilySize_bin) = 0.8212; LR+ET+GB 3-way vote = 0.8436; ET n_estimators 400->800 = 0.8436; decision threshold 0.45 = 0.8380; 5-seed bagging = 0.8436; CV-selected LR C=0.3 = 0.8380. ET criterion='entropy' produced byte-identical predictions to gini (no change in metric). Each was reverted to the incumbent.

**Changes from the parent.** The parent is the same LR+ExtraTrees soft-vote incumbent at w=0.5 with depth=6, leaf=4 (scored 0.8492). The best version is identical to the parent; all substantive changes attempted this round regressed, so the parent recipe was retained and re-verified.

**Artifacts & loading (in `work/`):**
- `work/model_blend_best.joblib`: dict with keys `lr`, `et` (full sklearn Pipelines including preprocessing), `w` (0.5), `n_estimators`, `threshold` (0.5), `lr_C` (1.0), `et_criterion` ('gini'). Load with `joblib.load("work/model_blend_best.joblib")`; predict via `w*lr.predict_proba(X)[:,1] + (1-w)*et.predict_proba(X)[:,1] >= threshold`, where `X` is the featurized DataFrame (FamilySize/IsAlone/Title/Embarked derived, raw columns selected).
- `predictions.csv`: 418-row test predictions (PassengerId, Survived), original test order.
- `work/val_predictions.csv`: 179-row validation predictions aligned to validation order.
- `work/metrics.json`: config, metric 0.8492, full perturbation ledger, pinned md5s.
- `work/README.txt`: inference instructions.

**Reproducibility.** Seed 42, CPU, n_jobs=4, no downloads; val/test predictions come from the same single model and were asserted byte-identical to the pinned md5s on reload.
experiments.suggestions:
**Observed weaknesses (evidence):**
- The 179-row holdout is tiny; a single row is worth ~0.0056 accuracy, so perturbations move the score by only 1-4 rows and are dominated by noise. Round-4 and round-18 CV gains on 712 rows (+0.003 to +0.007 in 5-fold) failed to transfer to the holdout (both scored ~0.838-0.844) — CV-based selection is not a reliable proxy here.
- Every added feature/model complexity (interactions, GradientBoosting, seed bagging, stronger ET) regressed; the incumbent is a stable optimum on this specific holdout.
- Threshold and criterion changes either regressed (0.45) or were prediction-identical (entropy), implying the model's decision boundary is already saturated for these features.

**Prioritized next experiments (hypotheses, not yet demonstrated):**
1. Genuine new signal, not model tuning: the strongest untested Titanic predictor is likely `Cabin` deck (first letter), currently dropped. A fit-safe deck feature (missing -> 'U') could add real information the current feature set lacks — test as a single controlled addition over the incumbent.
2. Family/ticket-group survival features: shared `Ticket` prefix and group-size interactions sometimes carry signal; test one at a time and only keep if it beats 0.8492 on the fixed holdout (guard against the observed overfitting-on-179 pattern).
3. If further tuning is pursued, consider that the evaluator's 712/179 split is the only reliable measuring stick — do not trust internal CV for final selection, since two CV-selected configs both regressed.
4. Do NOT re-run already-rejected perturbations (interactions, GB, more trees, threshold shift, seed-bag, LR C, criterion) — they have executed negative evidence.

**Lesson:** On this holdout the incumbent LR+ET (w=0.5, d=6, leaf=4) is the reproducible best; future rounds should either accept it as final or justify a *new-information* feature (e.g., Cabin deck) with a single controlled test rather than more hyperparameter search.

experiments.title: LR+ET + Cabin Deck blend
experiments.description:
Objective: binary classification of Titanic `Survived` (0/1) on the fixed local split. Best measured validation metric: Accuracy 0.8492 (engine-recorded), achieved by the incumbent LR+ExtraTrees soft-vote. That remained the best across every executed iteration.

Data & split (all executed):
- Read only `../input/data/train_data/train.csv` (712 rows), `../input/data/validation_data/validation.csv` (179 feature-only rows), `../input/data/predict_data/test.csv` (418 rows). No external data, no `gender_submission.csv`, never read validation labels.
- Fixed validation IDs frozen once to `work/val_ids.json` and asserted unchanged every round; train/val/test PassengerId sets asserted disjoint.

Preprocessing (fit on the 712 training rows only; val/test transform-only), embedded in each sklearn Pipeline's ColumnTransformer:
- FamilySize = SibSp+Parch+1; IsAlone = (FamilySize==1).
- Title via regex `,\s*([^.]+)\.`; Mlle/Ms→Miss, Mme→Mrs; titles with training count <10 → 'Rare' (rare set from full train).
- Embarked missing → 'M'.
- num [Pclass,SibSp,Parch,FamilySize,IsAlone] → SimpleImputer(median)+StandardScaler.
- af [Age,Fare] → SimpleImputer(median, add_indicator=True)+StandardScaler.
- cat [Sex,Embarked,Title] → SimpleImputer(constant 'M')+OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore').

Model (chosen = incumbent): w=0.5, ET n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, min_samples_leaf=4, gini, random_state=42, n_jobs=4; LR max_iter=2000, random_state=42. Blend prob = 0.5*p_LR + 0.5*p_ET; Survived = (prob ≥ 0.5). Model fit on all 712 training rows.

Validation evidence (executed):
- Incumbent external fixed split accuracy = 0.8492 (recorded by evaluator; best).
- Negative/regressed trials, all executed against the same fixed holdout and returned to incumbent:
  - w40 (CV-selected) → 0.8436 (reverted).
  - Threshold shift to 0.58 → 0.8268 (reverted).
  - Deck, GradientBoosting member, SexPclass+FareBand interactions, Title-conditioned Age imputation: no external gain / tied on internal/CV proxies; not adopted.
- Internal 20% stratified holdout and 5-fold/2×5 repeated CV were executed but did not transfer to the fixed external holdout (e.g., CV gains of +0.004 mapped to external losses).

Change from parent: the parent's best scored code is the same incumbent configuration (0.8492). This round tested six controlled single-factor variants (Cabin Deck feature, GradientBoosting third member, SexPclass/FareBand interactions, blend weight w=0.4/0.6, Title-conditioned Age imputation, decision threshold sweep). None improved the fixed external metric; the delivered model is unchanged from the parent's best, and the incumbent is delivered rather than any unverified/regressed variant.

Artifacts:
- `predictions.csv` — 418 rows, header `PassengerId,Survived`, test order preserved, int 0/1, no index.
- `work/val_predictions.csv` — 179 rows, aligned to validation.csv order.
- `work/model_best.joblib` — dict `{lr, et, w, depth, leaf, threshold, cols, title_rare}`.
- `work/metrics.json`, `work/comparison.csv`, `work/README.txt` — metrics, ledger, inference instructions.
- Loading: `m = joblib.load("work/model_best.joblib")`; featurize inputs (FamilySize, IsAlone, Title rare-map, Embarked NA→M); then `p = m["w"]*m["lr"].predict_proba(X[m["cols"]])[:,1] + (1-m["w"])*m["et"].predict_proba(X[m["cols"]])[:,1]; pred = (p >= m["threshold"]).astype(int)`.
experiments.suggestions:
Evidence-based weaknesses:
- Label-free proxies (internal 20% holdout, 5-fold and 2×5 repeated CV) consistently failed to transfer to the fixed 179-row holdout: CV +0.004 gains produced external losses (w40 → 0.8436, thr0.58 → 0.8268). This is the central obstacle — model selection without validation labels is unreliable here.
- The incumbent's frozen configuration (w=0.5, depth=6, leaf=4, threshold=0.5) is a strong local optimum on this split; small perturbations cost the >0.5pp needed to accept.

Lessons:
- Do not adopt internal/CV-selected variants when the acceptance rule is based on the fixed external holdout; every such adoption (w40, thr0.58) regressed. Only external-measured gains should change the delivered model.
- Cabin Deck, GradientBoosting, interactions, and Title-Age imputation were genuine hypotheses but produced no measurable external gain — treat as negative evidence and avoid re-testing.

Prioritized next experiments (hypotheses, unexecuted — must be scored on the fixed holdout before adoption):
1. Calibrated ensemble stacking: fit a meta-learner on out-of-fold LR+ET(+GB) probabilities via stratified CV inside the 712 training rows, then test whether the stack beats 0.8492 externally (higher value than hand-tuned blend weights).
2. Regularized/regularization-tuned LR (C sweep with ElasticNet via sag) and a shallower ET (max_depth=5) as separate single-factor external tests — if the external metric cannot be checked before delivery, keep incumbent.
3. Fair-Fare imputation and single-ticket group size. Treat as one controlled addition; reject unless it clears the >0.5pp external margin.
4. If more rounds remain, prioritize acquiring a proxy that correlates with the fixed holdout (e.g., a held-out fraction of the *external validation distribution* is not permitted — instead use nested CV with a stricter acceptance margin >1.5pp) so adopted changes are less likely to regress.
No further version has been executed that beats 0.8492; the incumbent should be delivered unless a new variant is externally measured to exceed it.
